THE DESIGN

Local foundations. Clear boundaries.

How ByteQuay connects GitHub review and local agent work without turning the desktop app into a remote execution service.

ON THIS PAGE Product intentArchitectureTrust & dataPrinciples

01 / PRODUCT INTENT

Keep the work and its purpose together.

ByteQuay connects repository context, development, review, and delivery in one macOS workspace. As agents write more code, ByteQuay helps people keep their understanding: explore the details they need, discuss the work and its assumptions, and merge with confidence.

The development-only Goal experiment clarifies the intended outcome. Epics organize related work. Development tasks, pull-request reviews, and cherry-picks carry changes forward while keeping their context close.

For everyday usage, explore the feature guides. The high-level product design describes the durable intent behind the experience.

02 / ARCHITECTURE

A desktop shell and one local backend.

React and TypeScript render the interface inside Electron. Electron owns native windows, browser views, and communication with a Spring Boot sidecar on localhost. SQLite stores durable application state.

React interface
↔
Electron
↔
Local backend
↔
SQLite + task files

Shared agent services coordinate conversations, approvals, and local working copies. Provider adapters connect that experience to Codex and Claude. GitHub and optional integrations remain external services.

The architecture document explains module responsibilities, data ownership, runtime boundaries, and tradeoffs.

03 / TRUST & DATA

Local work. Deliberate actions.

  • Local app data. ByteQuay stores all app data on the Mac, including conversations, reviews, settings, and working copies. The backend listens on localhost.
  • Separate working copies. Tasks use managed worktrees so their changes can be inspected independently. Worktree separation is not a security sandbox.
  • Explicit publication. GitHub writes require a direct action or an explicitly accepted automation scope. Reading and private discussion do not publish anything.
  • External services. GitHub, model providers, and optional integrations receive the requests needed for their features. Local-first does not mean offline inference.

04 / PRINCIPLES

Make the change understandable.

Keep intent, code, evidence, and discussion close. Distinguish an explanation from a verified result. Preserve useful context and uncertain work, and make the next action clear.

Extend the existing services when adding features. Add another system boundary only when a real ownership or dependency need justifies it.

The repository keeps two public design documents: product design and architecture. Feature instructions live in the user guide; implementation details live with code and tests.
